q: Why do photosystems contain several types of pigment (chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids) rather than chlorophyll a alone?
options: Each absorbs different wavelengths, widening the range of light energy that reaches the reaction centre
Only carotenoids are able to donate excited electrons to NADP, so they are essential in every photosystem
Chlorophyll b takes over from chlorophyll a whenever light intensity becomes very high
Multiple pigments let the leaf reflect every wavelength, protecting it from overheating
explanation: Chlorophyll a absorbs mainly blue-violet and red light; chlorophyll b absorbs slightly different blue and red wavelengths; carotenoids absorb blue-green light. Together they broaden the absorption spectrum, so more of the available light is captured and funnelled to the reaction centre – which is why the action spectrum of photosynthesis is broader than chlorophyll a's absorption spectrum.
